name: Brain Pial Arteriovenous Fistula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Identification of a direct arteriovenous fistula between pial arteries and cortical veins on cerebral angiography or MRI/MRA
Lack of an intervening nidus differentiating it from arteriovenous malformations
Neurological symptoms consistent with high-flow arteriovenous shunting such as hemorrhage or seizures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of direct arteriovenous fistula on imaging without nidus plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on advanced neuroimaging techniques; histopathology rarely required

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intracranial hemorrhage due to fistula rupture
pathognomonic.notes: Often presents as sudden severe headache or neurological deficit
searchTerms: bleeding inside skull due to fistula break

pathognomonic.notes: Audible bruit due to high-flow shunting

common.notes: Depends on location of fistula and hemorrhage
Due to venous hypertension or ischemia

occasional.notes: Due to venous congestion or hemorrhage
From mass effect or venous congestion
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain swelling

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to venous outflow obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain due to vein blockage
brain swelling from blocked venous outflow

laboratory: Generally normal; no specific laboratory markers
imaging: Digital subtraction angiography showing direct arteriovenous fistula without nidus
MRI/MRA demonstrating abnormal vascular shunting and dilated cortical veins
CT scan may show intracranial hemorrhage or venous congestion
genetic: No known genetic mutations specifically associated
other: Clinical auscultation may reveal cranial bruit
Histopathology rarely performed; confirms direct arterial to venous connection

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of a nidus on imaging
Fistula located in dural venous sinuses rather than pial arteries
Different clinical presentation and venous drainage patterns

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with neurological deficit
Signs of intracranial hemorrhage on imaging
references: Lasjaunias P, et al. Pial arteriovenous fistulas: clinical and angiographic features. Neurosurgery. 1996.
Matsubara S, et al. Brain pial arteriovenous fistulas: diagnosis and treatment. J Neurosurg. 2018.
Orphanet: Brain pial arteriovenous fistula. ORPHA:715292.
